questions.question: Evaluate the roles of skeletal muscles in the human body?
questions.solution_html:
• Skeletal muscles are voluntary muscles attached close to the skeleton. These
  • muscles are attached to the bones with the aid of a fibrous connective tissue called
  • tendon. The primary role of skeletal muscle is for the aid of locomotion and
  • movement. There are mainly two types of skeletal muscles red muscles and white
  • muscle. Red muscles are due to the red pigment called myoglobin, which is in high
  • amounts in the human body. These muscles are smaller in diameter and have a large
  • number of mitochondria in it. The myoglobin stores the oxygen, which is used by the
  • mitochondria for the synthesis of ATP. Red muscles have a large number of blood
  • capillaries in it. Unlike the red muscles, the white muscles are bigger in diameter
  • and have a small amount of myoglobin in it. They also have a smaller number of
  • mitochondria in it. Red fibres are suited for long term slow contraction white fibres
  • are suited for high fibre contraction.
  • (Function-(2 marks) Description -(1 mark))
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Design a weekly recovery plan for an athlete based on HRV and sleep tracking data.
questions.solution_html:
• Design a weekly recovery plan for an athlete based on HRV and sleep tracking data.
  • Ans-Consistent, high-quality sleep improves athletic performance, reaction times
  • and decision-making abilities.Aligning training and recovery periods with natural
  • circadian rhythms enhances recovery. For example, optimizing sleep by maintaining
  • a regular sleep schedule helps synchronize the circadian rhythm, leading to better
  • overall recovery.
  • Heart Rate Variability (HRV)
  • HRV can provide insights into an athlete’s autonomic nervous system balance and
  • recovery status. Monitoring HRV can help determine if an athlete is adequately recovered
  • or overtraining.
  • Sleep Tracking
  • Quality sleep is essential for recovery and performance. Using sleep tracking devices or
  • apps can help athletes understand their sleep patterns and identify areas for improvement.

questions.question: Explain the biochemical effects of thermotherapy
questions.solution_html:
• Ans-Thermotherapy involves applying heat to injured areas to relax muscles
  • increase blood flow, and promote tissue healing. The Biochemical effects
  • include
  • Vasodilation: Heat causes blood vessels to dilate, increasing blood flow to the
  • area, which helps deliver oxygen and nutrients to tissues for repair.
  • Enhanced Metabolism: Increases metabolic activity, promoting the removal
  • of waste products and accelerating the healing process.
  • Muscle Relaxation: Reduces muscle stiffness and spasms by relaxing muscle
  • fibres and improving flexibility.
  • ((1 mark) each)

questions.question: Illustrate the influence of hormones in sports and exercise
questions.solution_html:
• Hormones play a crucial role in regulating energy metabolism
  • muscle growth, recovery, and overall performance in sports. Key
  • hormones involved in sports performance include
  • Insulin
  • Function: Regulates blood glucose levels by facilitating glucose
  • uptake into cells, promotes glycogen storage, and inhibits fat
  • breakdown.
  • Importance: Post-exercise insulin response is critical
  • for glycogen replenishment and muscle recovery.
  • Glucagon
  • Function: Opposes insulin action by promoting glycogen breakdown and gluconeogenesis to increase blood glucose levels. glucose from liver glycogen stores.
  • Catecholamines (Adrenaline and Noradrenaline)
  • Function: Increase heart rate, blood pressure, and
  • energy availability by stimulating glycogenolysis and
  • lipolysis.
  • Importance: Essential for the fight-or-flight response
  • during high-intensity activities, enhancing performance
  • and focus.
  • Cortisol
  • Function: Increases gluconeogenesis, protein
  • breakdown, and fat mobilization; suppresses the
  • immune system.
  • Importance: Helps maintain energy supply during
  • prolonged stress or exercise but can impair recovery
  • and immune function if chronically elevated.
  • Growth Hormone (GH)
  • Function: Stimulates protein synthesis, muscle growth
  • and fat metabolism; promotes tissue repair.
  • Importance: Crucial for muscle development, recovery, and
  • adaptation to training.
  • Explain each((1 mark) for each)

questions.question: Evaluate the roles of skeletal muscles in the human body?
questions.solution_html:
• Skeletal muscles are voluntary muscles attached close to the skeleton. These
  • muscles are attached to the bones with the aid of a fibrous connective tissue called
  • tendon. The primary role of skeletal muscle is for the aid of locomotion and
  • movement. There are mainly two types of skeletal muscles red muscles and white
  • muscle. Red muscles are due to the red pigment called myoglobin, which is in high
  • amounts in the human body. These muscles are smaller in diameter and have a large
  • number of mitochondria in it. The myoglobin stores the oxygen, which is used by the
  • mitochondria for the synthesis of ATP. Red muscles have a large number of blood
  • capillaries in it. Unlike the red muscles, the white muscles are bigger in diameter
  • and have a small amount of myoglobin in it. They also have a smaller number of
  • mitochondria in it. Red fibres are suited for long term slow contraction white fibres
  • are suited for high fibre contraction.
  • (Function-(2 marks) Description -(1 mark))

questions.question: Explain the biochemical effects of thermotherapy
questions.solution_html:
• Ans-Thermotherapy involves applying heat to injured areas to relax muscles
  • increase blood flow, and promote tissue healing. The Biochemical effects
  • include
  • Vasodilation: Heat causes blood vessels to dilate, increasing blood flow to the
  • area, which helps deliver oxygen and nutrients to tissues for repair.
  • Enhanced Metabolism: Increases metabolic activity, promoting the removal
  • of waste products and accelerating the healing process.
  • Muscle Relaxation: Reduces muscle stiffness and spasms by relaxing muscle
  • fibres and improving flexibility.

questions.question: Illustrate the influence of hormones in sports and exercise
questions.solution_html:
• Hormones play a crucial role in regulating energy metabolism
  • muscle growth, recovery, and overall performance in sports. Key
  • hormones involved in sports performance include
  • Insulin
  • Function: Regulates blood glucose levels by facilitating glucose
  • uptake into cells, promotes glycogen storage, and inhibits fat
  • breakdown.
  • Importance: Post-exercise insulin response is critical
  • for glycogen replenishment and muscle recovery.
  • Glucagon
  • Function: Opposes insulin action by promoting glycogen breakdown and gluconeogenesis to increase blood glucose levels. glucose from liver glycogen stores.
  • Catecholamines (Adrenaline and Noradrenaline)
  • Function: Increase heart rate, blood pressure, and
  • energy availability by stimulating glycogenolysis and
  • lipolysis.
  • Importance: Essential for the fight-or-flight response
  • during high-intensity activities, enhancing performance
  • and focus.
  • Cortisol
  • Function: Increases gluconeogenesis, protein
  • breakdown, and fat mobilization; suppresses the
  • immune system.
  • Importance: Helps maintain energy supply during
  • prolonged stress or exercise but can impair recovery
  • and immune function if chronically elevated.
  • Growth Hormone (GH)
  • Function: Stimulates protein synthesis, muscle growth
  • and fat metabolism; promotes tissue repair.
  • Importance: Crucial for muscle development, recovery, and
  • adaptation to training.
  • Explain each((1 mark) for each)
